ranked_promos.posting_priority: POST FIRST (Day 1 Campaign Launch - Broad Reach)
ranked_promos.posting_rationale: This promo should be posted first across TikTok and Instagram Reels. It features primal, universal emotional stakes (altar abandonment and sister betrayal) that require zero prior knowledge to evoke instant anger and empathy. Its high hook-stopping power and ruthless cliffhanger cut maximize initial Click-Through Rate (CTR) and app install conversions for completely cold viewers.
ranked_promos.hook: The shocking revelation that Gerald is no longer waiting for Juliana immediately grabs attention, setting a tone of betrayal and despair.
ranked_promos.cliffhanger: The promo ends abruptly as Juliana's emotional turmoil peaks, leaving viewers desperate to know how she will respond to Gerald's cruel dismissal.
ranked_promos.why_it_works: This promo effectively captures raw emotion and conflict, compelling viewers to click for resolution.

ranked_promos.posting_rationale: Post this second to retarget users who engaged with the initial betrayal promo. It delivers the immediate emotional turnaround—a scarred, honorable soldier drops to one knee to defend Juliana before the sneering church guests. The cliffhanger cut on the wedding proposal compels viewers to binge Episode 2 and 3 immediately.

systemic_failure_modes.category: The 'Stage Direction' Illusion (Passive Action False Positive)
systemic_failure_modes.description: Script descriptions like 'Juliana clenches her knuckles with suppressed fury' or 'Her eyes fill with silent sorrow' read with high dramatic weight on paper. On screen, 4 seconds of silent physical reaction without rapid dialogue or camera movement translates to sluggish video pacing, triggering instant thumb scrolls.
systemic_failure_modes.impact: High bounce rate in first 2 seconds on TikTok / Instagram Reels.
systemic_failure_modes.mitigation: Enforce presence of punchy spoken dialogue or dynamic camera motion (extreme close-up / sudden snap) within the first 1.5 seconds.

systemic_failure_modes.description: Episodes 30-50 feature intense confrontations, but they hinge on intricate subplots (e.g., poisoned dowries, secondary noble factions, forged wills). The tool detects explosive keywords ('poison', 'traitor', 'proof'), but cold viewers scrolling social feeds have zero emotional investment in secondary characters.
systemic_failure_modes.impact: High initial click-through but catastrophic drop-off before 10 seconds; low app installation conversion.
systemic_failure_modes.mitigation: Apply a steep decay penalty to episodes beyond Episode 20 for top-of-funnel ads, reserving them strictly for mid-campaign retargeting.

systemic_failure_modes.description: Nearly every episode ends with a variation of 'Solemn low-pitched string drone swells to an ominous cliffhanger peak. Cut to black.' The tool can be tricked into picking a dull 30-second lead-up simply because the terminal SFX cue contains the literal word 'cliffhanger'.
systemic_failure_modes.impact: Promos that start weakly but end with a loud boom and cut to black, boring viewers long before the cliffhanger arrives.
systemic_failure_modes.mitigation: Couple cliffhanger scoring with dialogue tension and unresolved character questions, rather than relying solely on SFX cues.

systemic_failure_modes.description: Stitching two segments from different scenes or episodes (e.g. Cathedral altar to rainy woods) can create jarring tonal dissonance. Without a crossfade or audio bridge, a cold viewer experiences cognitive whiplash.
systemic_failure_modes.impact: Viewer confusion regarding character location, wardrobe, and timeline.
systemic_failure_modes.mitigation: Restrict stitched promos to segments that share identical location headings or involve immediate cause-and-effect character actions.

systemic_failure_modes.description: Automated time boundaries that cut off an actor mid-breath, mid-sentence, or right as the background score resolves rather than holding the unresolved tension.
systemic_failure_modes.impact: The promo feels mechanically truncated or defective.
systemic_failure_modes.mitigation: Snap candidate boundaries strictly to beat ends and use LLM offset refinement to ensure natural sentence cadences.

recommendations: Always preview the first 2 seconds on actual mobile vertical frame (9:16) to verify that physical action reads dynamically without relying on reading stage directions.
For cold acquisition on TikTok, prioritize Episodes 1-4 promos where the emotional premise is universally self-explanatory (wedding altar abandonment).
When using stitched promos across different locations, add a quick 0.5s audio bridge or whoosh sound effect so viewers perceive it as a deliberate trailer cut rather than a playback error.
Avoid using promos from late episodes (> Ep 30) for cold audiences; deploy them exclusively as retargeting ads to viewers who have already completed Episode 5.
